records.c: The event's entry, from the resident menu's table: shows the event's title screen through the resident $C540 (A = 1, this event).

Banks the KERNAL and BASIC ROMs out, points the NMI vector at nmi_rti ($34DA) and the IRQ vector at irq_entry ($11D4), turns on the raster interrupt at line 0, picks video bank 1 with the screen at $4000 and the character set at $4800, and enables interrupts.
Sets up the sprites ($20C6), builds the field's character set ($235A) and the crowd's ($2541).

A new contest: clears the screen ($1FA4), silences the SID ($33E4), plays effect 7, draws the top panel ($2E3A), and clears the throw count ($1D0D), the two best distances ($1E69-$1E6C), the computer flag ($1538) and the best run-up speed ($153C); no player is the computer yet ($1539 = $FF).
The first player of a round of throws.

One throw: resets the thrower ($1D0E), draws the field ($1FC8), the speed bar ($2E2C), stands the thrower (sequence 0), sets sprite multicolour 2 (light red for player one, yellow for player two), draws the body, clears the distance panel and the distance, and waits for the player ($1C8C).

The throw's loop, once a frame: waits for the bottom of the screen, runs the run-up speed and the head's fall ($1AC4), moves the flying head ($1B88), switches to the landing screen when the head flies off the right edge ($1F86), then runs the thrower's state ($14BC), draws the head ($117A) and the body ($1F7D), places the foul line ($1F62), scrolls the crowd ($1EFD) and shows the distance ($2C94) and the speed bar.
In the demo, fire on any device goes back to the start of the contest.
The head has flown off the right edge: to the landing screen.
Loops until the throw is over ($1525).
In the demo, after the throw: up to 150 frames for fire on any device; either way back to the start of the contest.

A foul shows "NO THROW" (message 5). Then 50 frames' pause, the throw's result ($1DB4), and the next player; after both, the next throw of three; after three each, the winner ($1E72) and a new contest.
Redraws the body's sprites when its frame ($152C) has changed since the last drawing ($1179): the hi-res layer ($20FC) and the multicolour layer ($213F).
The body frame drawn last.

Redraws the head's sprites when its frame has changed ($119B): the frame is the head's angle ($1526), or, at angle 8 with the ears moving ($153E), $24 plus the ear frame. Nothing while $1526 is negative, before the head is picked up.
The head frame drawn last.
Left over and called by nothing: a test loop that draws the head through all 32 angles, one every two frames, with the ears flapping, for ever.
head_spin's count.
$FF once the head has been thrown: the bands stop placing the body's sprites, which the head then uses.
The raster band the interrupt is in, 0 to 5.
The next band's raster ninth bit, ORed into $D011.
The six bands' raster lines, two bytes each (line, ninth bit): $5A, $79, $90, $9A, $B8 and 256.
The bands' ninth bits, read with the lines at $11C8.
The raster interrupt: saves A, X and Y at $1A-$1C, sends a BRK to the resident code at $0810, and otherwise jumps to the band's handler through the JMP at $11E3.
The BRK way out: jumps to the resident code at $0810.
The JMP to the band's handler, its operand rewritten from band_handlers at the end of each band.
The low byte of band_jump's operand.
The high byte of band_jump's operand.
The six band handlers: $11F2, $120F, $1222, $1287, $12A3 and $12EB.
The band handlers' high bytes, read with the low bytes at $11E6.
Line $5A: multicolours grey and blue, the top rows' fine scroll ($1537), light blue background.
Line $79: the crowd's character set at $5000 and its fine scroll ($1536).

Line $90: places the body's top four sprites (0, 1, 4 and 5) at row $92, X = $152B x 8 plus the scroll offset $1956, with the ninth bits set when it passes 255, and expands sprites 0, 1, 4 and 5 vertically; pointers $80, $81, $84 and $85. Skipped once the head is thrown.
Line $9A: green background, the field's character set at $4800, no fine scroll.
Line $B8: places the body's lower four sprites (2, 3, 6 and 7) at row $BA, all eight expanded vertically; pointers $82, $83, $86 and $87. Skipped once the head is thrown.

Line 256: checks RUN/STOP ($34DB), places all eight sprites as the head, 2 x 2 sprites in two layers, at ($1530, $1533) with pointers $88-$8F, sets the top panel's colours (yellow background, multicolours orange and white), then runs the timers ($13B5), reads the controls ($2BB3) and plays the sound ($334D).
Every band ends here: acknowledges the interrupt, steps to the next band, sets its raster line and handler, and restores A, X and Y.

Once a frame: counts down the game's timers. Three run on the step $1433 (the anim tick at $1429, the scroll tick at $142A, the distance tick at $142B); two count frames (the angle tick $142C every 10, the spin tick $142D every $1434). Each sets its flag to $FF when it runs out. Every 10 frames it also inverts the cursor character's rows at $4AD9.
Frames to the cursor's next flash.
The timers' flags, $FF when each has run out: animation ($1429), scroll ($142A), distance ($142B), angle ($142C) and spin ($142D).
The scroll tick's flag.
The distance tick's flag.
The angle tick's flag.
The spin tick's flag.
The three stepped timers' counts ($142E-$1430), the angle timer ($1431) and the spin timer ($1432).
The scroll tick's count.
The distance tick's count.
The angle timer's count, 10 frames.
The spin timer's count.
The stepped timers' step, set from the run-up speed ($1994): faster running, faster steps.
The spin timer's reload: how many frames between the head's turns.
The body's ten animation sequences: 0 standing, 1 and 2 the first strides, 3 and 4 the running strides, 5 the plant, 6 the step into the throw, 7 the throw, 8 and 9 walking.
The sequences' addresses, high bytes, read with the low bytes at $1435.
The sequences, each a list of (step, frame) pairs, ended by $FF: the step is added to the body's column ($152B), the frame is the body's picture. Sequence 0: one step, frame 1.
Sequence 3, a running stride on the spot while the crowd scrolls: frames 7, 8, 9, 0 and 1.
Sequence 4, the other running stride on the spot: frames 2 to 6.
Sequence 5, the plant: frames $A, $B and $C.
Sequence 6, the step into the throw: one step, frame $D.
Sequence 7, the throw: frames $E, $F, $F and $10.
Sequence 8, a walking stride: frames $18, $19, $1A (three times), $11 and $12, a step each.
Sequence 9, the other walking stride: frames $13, $14, $15 (three times), $16 and $17, a step each.
Sequence 1, the first stride: frames 7, 8, 9 (three times), 0 and 1, a step each.
Sequence 2, the second stride: frames 2, 3, 4 (three times), 5 and 6, a step each.
The thrower's state, 0 to 12, an index into state_table.
Runs the thrower's state routine through the JMP at $14CD.
The JMP to the state routine, its operand rewritten from state_table.
The low byte of state_jump's operand.
The high byte of state_jump's operand.

The thirteen state routines: 0 standing ($14EA), 1 and 2 running ($1545), 3 the plant ($1602), 4 choosing the angle ($162D), 5 the step into the throw ($1678), 6 the throw ($1693), 7 the head in flight ($16A8), 8 landing ($17DF), 9 tipping over ($183C), 10 a pause ($1871), 11 after the landing ($187B), 12 the walk ($18F8).
The state routines' high bytes, read with the low bytes at $14D0.

State 0, standing: shows the speed bar. The human player's fire starts the throw at once ($15DB). Otherwise, while the speed is 0 nothing happens; once it is not, the running starts (state 1, sequence 1), with the crowd scrolling at once if the runner is already past the first two strides ($1520).
Starts the crowd scrolling.
$FF while the speed bar shows and the run-up speed counts.
The thrower's controls, a 0 bit for each held: up (bit 0), down (1), left (2), right (3), fire (4).
The run-up speed, 0 to $FF; once thrown, the head's forward speed.
The head's rising or falling speed, 16 bits, $151F the high byte.
The rising or falling speed's high byte.
The stride count: 1 and 2 the first strides, then 3 and 4 in turn.
$FF while running: the crowd scrolls.
The speed lost each frame: 1, 4 past the line's mark, 0 on the walk.
$FF when the human pressed fire during a stride: the throw starts at its end.
$FF for a foul: no throw.
$FF when the throw has ended.
The head's angle and frame: 8 level, 0 straight up, on round to $1F as it turns; $FF before the head is picked up.
$FF while the head rises, 1 once it falls.
The angle a tipping head comes to rest at: 8 or $16.
The tipping head's step, +1 or -1.
$FF while the head flies.
The body's column on the screen.
The body's frame.
Set to $FF at the throw and cleared at each throw's start; read by nothing.
Bit 7 set when the head has landed.
The head's X, sub-pixels.
The head's X ($1530) and its ninth bit ($1531).
The head's X ninth bit.
The head's height, sub-pixels.
The head's height on the screen: $C5 is the ground.
The track position's sub-steps.
The runner's or head's track position: the foul line at $46.
The crowd's fine scroll, 7 to 0.
The top rows' fine scroll.
$FF in the demo.
The player the computer throws for: 0 player one, 1 player two, $FF neither.
The computer's pace: the speed it runs up to.
The angle the computer throws at.
The fastest human run-up of the contest, which sets the computer's pace.
$FF once DOWN has flapped the ears, until UP.
The ears' frame: 0 still, 1 down, 2 up; 3 and 4 as the head bounces away.
The head's forward speed at the throw.
The frames a flap's extra speed lasts.
The computer's frames to its next flap.
The height under which the computer starts the turn.
Gravity, 16 bits: $1543 low, $1544 high.
Gravity's high byte.

States 1 and 2, running: moves the runner on along the track ($1958); past track position $45 it is state 2 and the speed falls four times as fast. The computer throws within 8 of the line ($46). The human's fire during a stride throws at its end ($1523), in state 1 only. At the end of each stride comes the next sequence, 1 and 2 for the first two strides, then 3 and 4 in turn with the crowd scrolling; in state 2 the runner carries on until stopped, and has thrown nothing ("NO THROW").
Starts the throw: keeps the fastest run-up ($153C, which sets the computer's pace), stops the scrolling, state 3, steps at $40, effect 1, sequence 5 (the plant).
State 3, at the end of the plant: the head's angle starts at 8 (level), its timer at 10, the head at ($7A, $33) by the body, state 4 and effect 5 (the charging hum).

State 4, choosing the angle: while the human holds FIRE the angle goes down by one every 10 frames, from 8 (level) towards 0 (straight up), and throws by itself at 0; releasing FIRE throws. The computer throws when the angle reaches its choice ($153B). The throw: works out the head's speeds from the run-up and the angle ($19EF) and its spin ($19C2), sets gravity to $0100, state 5, silence, sequence 6.
State 5, at the end of the step: the head leaves ($1967), state 6, sequence 7 (the throw).
State 6: the head's whistle, pitched by its height ($2F6E); at the end of the throw, state 7, the headless body drawn into the screen ($2054) and its sprites handed to the head ($11C5).

State 7, the head in flight, until it lands ($152E): the whistle; while the head is level (angle 8) the ears are steered ($16FE) until FIRE sets it turning ($16E0), and once turning it turns by one every $1434 frames ($17C8). The computer flaps every 15 frames and starts the turn when the head drops below the height it chose ($1542).
The computer: once the head's height above the ground ($C5 less $1533) is under its choice ($1542), it starts the turn.
FIRE: the head starts to turn, back to the throw's speed ($153F), gravity $0100, a turn every 10 frames.

The ears, with the head level: the human's UP and DOWN, or the computer's flap count ($1541, a flap every 15 frames). DOWN (ear frame 1) flaps them, once a stroke ($153D): the speed rises by $28 (to at most $FF) for 10 frames ($1540) and gravity falls to $0064, creeping back up while DOWN is held. UP (ear frame 2) readies the next stroke: the speed goes back to the throw's and gravity rises to $0200. Neither: ear frame 0, gravity $0100.
Turns the head one angle on (modulo 32) each time the spin timer runs out.

State 8, the head lands: an angle from $0C to $0F sticks it in by the nose (effect 2, the angle moved on $14 to the stuck frames) and the throw counts. Any other angle is a foul ($1524): it tips over to lie on its side, to angle 8 under $0C or $16 from $10, one turn at a time from every 6 frames (effect 6).
State 9, tipping over: one angle each time the spin timer runs out until it reaches $1528, then effect 4.
State 10: a pause of 100 frames, counted by twos.
State 10, waiting out the pause.

State 11: a throw that landed on the first screen ends here ($1525). On the landing screen, unless it was a foul, the head bounces off again with the ears flapping until it is off the right edge, and then the body walks on (state 12, sequence 8).
Frames between the ears' frames as the head bounces away.
State 12, the walk: the body walks on the spot at the left edge for four sequences (8 and 9 in turn), then walks across; the throw ends when it reaches column $2B.
The walk's sequence count, $80 when done.
$FF stops the distance counting, once the head has landed.
The body's sprite X offset, $20 at the start and 0 on the landing screen.
$FF once the head has bounced away: the landing screen is not switched again.
Each time the distance tick runs out, moves the runner one step on along the track ($1535).
The head leaves the hand: in flight ($152A), at X = body column x 8 + $32, height $7A, sub-pixels cleared, and the runner's track position moves on 6.
Sets the stepped timers' step from the speed: the faster the run, the shorter the step ($19A2, by speed / 8).
The stepped timers' steps by speed / 8: $7F standing, down to $10 at full speed.
Sets the spin rate: the rising speed divided by the angle's distance from level ((8 - angle) x 2), times two, and at least 6 frames; a level throw spins slowest ($FE).
set_spin's divisor.

Works out the head's speeds at the throw: rising speed $151F = run-up speed x sine(angle) / 32 + $14, forward speed $151D = run-up speed x cosine(angle) / 16 + $14 (to at most $FF), also kept at $153F; and sets the head rising ($1527).
Returns run-up speed ($151D) times the table entry at ($06) for the angle, divided by 16; 0 when the entry is 0.
scale's product, two bytes.
scale's product, high byte: the result.
The forward share by angle, 0 (straight up) to 8 (level): 0, 3, 6, 9, $B, $D, $F, $10, $10; and from $1A68 the rising share, $10 at angle 0 down to 0 at angle 8.
Starts animation sequence A: points $04/$05 at it and takes its first step.

When the animation tick has run out, takes the sequence's next step: moves the body by its step and sets its frame; frames 1 and 6 of a stride (and the walking frames $12 and $17) play the footstep (effect 3). Returns carry set at the end of the sequence.
The place in the sequence.

While the speed bar shows: the human gains speed for each new direction of LEFT or RIGHT after the other, more when slow (4 plus a share of what is left), the computer one a frame up to its pace ($153A); both lose the friction ($1522) each frame. Then, with the head rising, takes gravity off its rising speed until it turns over and falls, or adds gravity to its falling speed (to at most $FFFF).
The computer: one more speed a frame, up to its pace ($153A).
The last of LEFT and RIGHT the human pressed.

Once a frame while the head flies: X ($1530/$1531, with sub-pixels $152F) moves on by the forward speed x 4 / 256; past X = $12C the landing screen is due ($1C45). The height ($1533, sub-pixels $1532) moves by the rising or falling speed; at $C5 the head has landed ($152E). The track position moves on by half the forward speed, and once it is past the foul line ($46) the distance is counted.
Adds the forward speed / 8, through the BCD table at $1C4C, to the distance in centimetres ($1C46) and metres ($1C47), unless the head has landed.
move_head's work byte.
$FF when the head has flown past the right edge: the landing screen is due.
The throw's distance in BCD: centimetres ($1C46) and metres ($1C47).
The distance's metres.
Four bytes cleared at each throw and read by nothing.
The second of the four bytes nothing reads.
The third.
The fourth.
The numbers 0 to $62 in BCD, for count_distance.

Before each throw: if the computer throws, its turn ($1CCB). Otherwise waits for fire to be let go, shows "PLAYER ONE (or TWO) READY PRESS FIRE", and flashes the player's panel ($2F87) until a device's fire is pressed; that device is the player's ($2C1F). Then shows FIRST, SECOND or LAST THROW.
No fire within 256 frames on the first throw: for player one, the demo starts ($1CFA); for player two, the computer takes player two's place ($1539 = 1). On later throws it goes on waiting.
The computer's turn: chooses its pace and angle ($1D7F), shows "COMPUTERS THROW", and waits 50 frames.
The demo ($1538 = $FF): the computer plays player one, "DEMO MODE".
The player throwing: 0 player one, 1 player two.
The throw, 0 to 2.

Clears the thrower's state for a throw: speed, track position, sequence, flags and the head's place; friction 1, the last direction $0C, the head's angle $FF (not picked up) and the body's offset $20.
$FF on the landing screen.
The foul line's screen column: $46 less the track position, plus 3, or plus the body's column while running.
The demo's computer: a pace of at least $80 and an angle from 0 to 7.
The computer's choice for a throw: a pace of the best human run-up plus $14, from $80 to $F5; an angle of 4, 5 or 6 (5 twice as often); and a height for the ears of $28 to $37.

After a throw: keeps the distance as the player's best if it is longer, unless it was a foul. Then writes the result on the top panel in the throw's row and the player's column (from $1E56): the throw number or a cross for a foul, a gap, the metres, a point and the centimetres, with effect 8, and waits 100 frames.
The result's screen address for each throw and player: throw 1 at $403E and $4047, throw 2 at $4066 and $406F, throw 3 at $408E and $4097.
The result addresses' high bytes.
The result's seven characters as they are built.
Each player's best distance in BCD (centimetres, metres): player one's ($1E69), player two's ($1E6B).
Player one's best, metres.
Player two's best, centimetres.
Player two's best, metres.
1 when the computer threw in this contest: player two's best is then not kept as a record.
The longest throws kept from contest to contest, in BCD: player one's ($1E6E) and player two's ($1E70).
Player one's record, metres.
Player two's record, centimetres.
Player two's record, metres.

After the third throws: keeps each player's best as their record if longer (not player two's against the computer), then compares the two bests and shows "THE CONTEST IS A DRAW" or the winner. The test checks the metres' difference only after the borrow: with the metres level, player two wins on centimetres, but player one ahead on centimetres is called a draw. Then 100 frames, "PRESS FIRE TO PLAY AGAIN", and up to 1024 frames for fire.
The computer is in the contest: player two's record is left alone.

While running ($1521), each time the scroll tick runs out: scrolls the crowd a pixel; at the end of a character, moves rows 9 to 12 one character left and adds the next column from the crowd's strip, and the top rows' fine scroll ($1537) creeps down to 0.
Before the landing screen and while running: works out the foul line's column, and draws or clears it ($2C20).
Draws the body unless on the landing screen.
The head has flown off the right edge: it comes back in at X = $18; the landing screen ($1D6A) has no foul line and the crowd moves on.
Clears the screen to character 0, colour RAM 8 for its first 256 cells and 9 for the rest (multicolour black and white).

Draws the field: clears rows 14 to 19, lays the track's edges (characters $5C on row 20 and $5D on row 22) with a blank row between, blanks rows 6 and 7 in white, puts three characters ($96-$98) at $40F5, $411D and $411E, sets the crowd's and top rows' fine scroll to 7, clears the foul line's rows ($201C) and draws the crowd ($2F13).
Blanks rows 14 to 19 and 21, and redraws the track's edges on rows 20 and 22.
Blanks rows 20 to 22, the track, on the landing screen.
Draws the headless body into the screen where it stands, from row 14 at column $152B + 1, from the characters at $209E: six rows of five, then two of three. Not on the landing screen.
The headless body's characters, $0B to $32: eight rows of five, of which the last two rows show three.
All eight sprites on, 4 to 7 multicolour; colours: 0-3 blue, 4-7 grey; sprite multicolours grey and light grey; border grey; multicolour text on.

Draws body frame A into sprites $80-$83 at $6000 (the hi-res layer): the frame's data from body_frames ($2185) in two halves, each 20 rows of five bytes split three and two between a pair of sprites, the third byte of the right one and the last row cleared ($2283).
draw_body_hires's half count.
Draws the multicolour layer of body frame A, from entry A + 27 of body_frames, into sprites $84-$87 at $6100.
draw_body_multi's half count.
The body's 27 frames, two layers each: the hi-res layers (entries 0 to 26) then the multicolour layers (27 to 53), each 200 bytes from $6400 on.
The body frames' addresses, high bytes, read with the low bytes at $2185.
The body frames' addresses from entry 32.
A 55th entry, $8E30, where the head's frames start; nothing reads it.

Draws head frame A into sprites $88-$8B at $6200 (the hi-res layer): 128 bytes from $8E30 + A x 128, in two halves of five blank rows and sixteen of four bytes, three to the left sprite and one to the right ($22E7).
draw_head_hires's half count.
Draws the multicolour layer of head frame A, 128 bytes from $A2B0 + A x 128, into sprites $8C-$8F at $6300.
draw_head_multi's half count.
Copies 20 rows of five bytes from ($0E) into a sprite pair, three bytes to ($10) and two to ($12) with its third byte cleared, then clears a 21st row.
Clears five rows of a sprite pair at ($10) and ($12), then copies 16 rows of four bytes from ($0E), three to the left sprite and one to the right with the rest cleared.
Waits for the raster to pass line 256: the bottom of the screen.
Builds characters $01 onwards at $4808 from the picture at $23B1: 80 rows of five bytes, five characters across, so ten character rows of five.
The LDA operand build_field_chars moves on five bytes a row.
The high byte of build_field_chars's LDA operand.
build_field_chars's row count.
The picture build_field_chars cuts into characters: 80 rows of five bytes.

Builds the crowd's character set at $5000: four character rows of 64, written as strips seven characters wide and 32 rows deep from the patterns at $25DF, each strip the pattern its entry in the list at $25D6 names (224 bytes each), until $FF.
The LDA operand build_crowd_chars moves on through the patterns.
The high byte of build_crowd_chars's LDA operand.
build_crowd_chars's row count.
build_crowd_chars's place in the strip list.
The order of the crowd's strips: 1, 2, 0, 3, 1, 0, 1, 3, then $FF: eight strips, 56 characters a row.
The crowd's four patterns, 0 to 3: strips of 32 rows of seven bytes.

Reads the three fire buttons: the up-arrow key (keyboard row 6, column 6), joystick one's fire and joystick two's fire. Returns carry set and A = 0, 1 or 2 for the first one held, carry clear when none is.
fire_device's saved X.
Shows message A on the bottom row: scrolls the old one off two characters a frame for 19 frames, then types the new one a character every two frames with a cursor ($5B) after it.
Left over and read by nothing: a list of numbers 0 to $0D in groups, ended by $FF.
show_message's scroll count.
Five bytes nothing reads.
The addresses of the 12 messages, numbered from 0.
The message addresses' high bytes.
Two bytes between the table and the messages, read by nothing.
Message 0, "PLAYER ONE READY  PRESS FIRE", ended by $FF.
Message 1, "PLAYER TWO READY  PRESS FIRE", ended by $FF.
Message 2, "FIRST THROW", ended by $FF.
Message 3, "SECOND THROW", ended by $FF.
Message 4, "LAST THROW", ended by $FF.
Message 5, "NO THROW", ended by $FF.
Message 6, "THE CONTEST IS A DRAW", ended by $FF.
Message 7, "PLAYER ONE IS THE WINNER", ended by $FF.
Message 8, "PLAYER TWO IS THE WINNER", ended by $FF.
Message 9, "PRESS FIRE TO PLAY AGAIN", ended by $FF.
Message 10, "COMPUTERS THROW", ended by $FF.
Message 11, "DEMO MODE", ended by $FF.
Message 12, "STOP TO QUIT ANY KEY TO CONTINUE", ended by $FF; it is not in the table and nothing shows it.

Reads the player's device ($2C1F) into $151C: joystick one or two as the port reads, or the keyboard as a joystick: @ up, : down, H left, K right and the up-arrow key fire, a 0 bit for each held. The manual gives K as left and H as right.
read_controls's work byte.
The thrower's device: 0 keyboard, 1 joystick one, 2 joystick two.

The foul line: at its column ($1D6B) under $26, draws it down rows 20 to 22 (characters $3F and $40, $5E for the bottom) and blanks the rest of each row to the right; once it has gone, on the landing screen, clears the track ($2043).
The seven-segment patterns of the digits 0 to 9, then six more nothing asks for.
While the head flies: draws the distance as four seven-segment digits at $4032, $4034, $4037 and $4039 with the point at $405E and $4086.
A spare zero byte.
Draws the seven-segment pattern A as a digit two characters wide and three high at the screen address X, Y ($40XX): each cell's character is $5F plus the segments it shows.
draw_digit's and draw_bar's work byte.
Blanks the distance panel, rows 1 to 3 from column $32, and its colours.
Draws a bar of six cells at ($0A) for the value A: A / 4 less A / 16 (at most $2F); full cells, one part cell ($70 plus the remainder), blanks; and colours the cells red.
Not reached: a full bar, $2F, filled with character $76.
draw_bar's level ($2E2A) and quarter ($2E2B).
draw_bar's quarter.
Draws the speed bar at $4052 for the run-up speed ($151D).
Draws the top panel, rows 0 to 4, from the 200 bytes at $2E4B, each plus $53.
The top panel's characters less $53, five rows of 40: the speed box on the left, the three throws' box for each player and the distance box.

Draws the crowd's four rows (9 to 12) from its scroll place ($2F66), each row $40 characters on from the one above, moves the place on 5, works out the foul line's column and draws it; on the landing screen also shifts rows 6 and 7 ($2F52).
Moves the first ten characters of rows 6 and 7 one left.
The crowd's scroll place: the first column's character.
A random byte: the byte at the start of a page, a page further on each call (the LDA operand's high byte steps).
The high byte of random's LDA operand, which steps a page each call.
The head's whistle on voice 1: its pitch $C8 less the head's height, a pulse wave with the gate on.
Every 10 frames, flashes the waiting player's box in the top panel (player one's colour RAM at $D83D, player two's at $D846, three rows of seven) between black and yellow.
Stops the flash with the box black.
Nonzero once an effect has been started.
Each voice's script finished: 1 when it has.
Voice 2's script finished.
Voice 3's script finished.

Once a frame, for each of the three voices: counts down the note's length, reads the next script entry when it ends, gates the note off one tick before, and slides the pitch by the instrument's step every so many ticks, reversing it when the vibrato count runs out.

Once a frame: RUN/STOP (keyboard row 7, column 7) quits to the menu ($34EB).

RUN/STOP's way out: banks the I/O in, hands the records ($1E6E-$1E71, when either is nonzero) to the resident code at $B824 and the computer flag ($1E6D) to $B82C, calls the resident $B839 with $02 = 3 when $B800 is 0, then restores the ROMs, blanks the screen, resets the KERNAL's I/O, and loads HARRY, the menu, from disk ($35A1); on an error it prints "ERROR READING DISK... ENSURE CORRECT DISK IS IN DRIVE", waits 200 frames and tries again. Then $FF = 4 and on to the menu at $0E90.
The disk error message in PETSCII (clear screen, two returns, "ERROR READING DISK...", two returns, "ENSURE CORRECT DISK IS IN DRIVE"), ended by $FF.
Loads "0:HARRY" from device 8 with its own load address, through the resident loader at $0800; returns carry set on an error.
The file name, "0:HARRY".
